summary: Fixed three issues from the PR's Greptile security review: unauthenticated MCP HTTP transport, a snapshot-label timestamp collision, and plaintext-argv token input.
reason: Greptile scored the PR 0/5 and flagged: (1) the generated MCP HTTP transport had no ingress authentication, letting any network caller invoke destructive tools (collection/tenant delete) using the server's own credentials; (2) unlabeled schema snapshots used second-resolution timestamps, so two snapshots within the same second silently overwrote each other; (3) `auth set-token <token>` required the token as a positional argument, exposing it via process list and shell history. Fixed the HTTP transport to require a WEAVIATE_COLLECTIONS_MCP_TOKEN bearer token (checked with constant-time comparison) and default to loopback-only binding; switched the snapshot default label to nanosecond resolution; made `auth set-token` accept the token via stdin (recommended) while keeping the positional form for backward compatibility.
validated_outcome: Confirmed: `--transport http` without WEAVIATE_COLLECTIONS_MCP_TOKEN now refuses to start (exit 2); `auth set-token` works via both stdin piping and the legacy positional form; go build/go vet clean.
